recipes.name: Restaurant-Style Beef and Broccoli
ingredients_raw: 0.75 pound beef round steak, cut into 1/8-inch thick strips
3 tablespoons vegetable oil, plus more if needed
1 thin slice of fresh ginger root

steps.text: Whisk oyster sauce, sherry, sesame oil, soy sauce, sugar, and cornstarch together in a bowl; stir until sugar has dissolved.
Place steak in a shallow bowl. Pour oyster sauce mixture over meat and stir to coat; cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat. Add ginger and garlic; let sizzle for about 1 minute to flavor oil, then remove and discard.
Stir in broccoli. Toss and stir until bright green and almost tender, 5 to 7 minutes. Remove broccoli from the wok and set aside.
Add a little more oil to the wok, if needed, then add beef with marinade.
Stir and toss until sauce thickens and turns shiny and meat is no longer pink, about 5 minutes.
Return broccoli to the wok; stir until heated through, about 3 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Restaurant-Style Beef and Broccoli
raw_recipe.description: This beef and broccoli recipe with ginger and garlic is Chinese stir-fry food at its best. It's quick and easy to make and delicious served over rice.

review.reviewBody: Familiar with Chinese cooking, I recognized this as a classic blend of seasonings and ingredients as well as an accurate cooking method. Therefore, I prepared this exactly as written - and it was perfect, just as I had anticipated it would be. My only criticism, and the only thing I did differently, was that the recipe calls for round steak, which I don't think is suited for this style of cooking. I used a New York strip steak, but tenderloin or sirloin would have worked well too. The ingredients in the marinade are so traditional and so key to the dish that I don't really see how you could make any changes and get a fair result. This was just delicious and made hubs and I members of "the clean plate club." Just a tip - if you partially freeze the steak for a half hour or so until semi-firm you will find this so much easier to cut into the thin slice so necessary for this style of cooking.

This is delicious, I made one change because I have a friend who worked in a Chinese restaurant for years and she told me the secret to always tender beef even using tough cuts of meat is to cut the beef into strips then place in a plastic bag overnight with 1/2 t baking soda. Before preparing the recipe, rinse the beef off twice and dry on paper towels. Other than that difference, I followed the recipe to a T. Next time might add a few dried chilies, because I like the heat, but the sauce is wonderful!

OK... if you don't like people who don't follow the recipe, yet review it anyway - then don't read any further! I followed the cooking instructions, but I didn't have some of the ingredients, so I substituted, using what I had on hand. I didn't have oyster sauce or sherry, so I used hoisin and extra amounts of soy sauce, and I substituted brown sugar for the white - just because. Instead of fresh, I used powdered ginger, onion, and garlic, which I added to the marinade. I marinated the meat for 2 hours, which was good - but overnight would be better. I used the Normandy frozen veggie blend (broccoli, cauliflower, carrots) from Sam's and added a large sweet onion. I don't measure anything - just guesstimate, dump, and taste-test until it suits me. It turned out very tasty! I'll make this version as written when I have all the ingredients - but, I'll be doing my own version again too! If this one is half as good as mine, I'll be happy happy!
Add one teaspoon of baking soda per pound of meat and let marinate for about 3 hours. No more tough steak! Other than that follow recipe as written.

Velvet your beef beforehand for that restaurant texture! It couldn't be easier- place sliced beef into a bowl and sprinkle with ~tsp baking soda and salt. Let sit 15 mins and then rinse. You can then skip the marinade and jump straight to cooking. I do this for every stir-fry, with all kinds of meat. (Also I only gave this recipe a 4 because you should use Shaoxing wine instead of sherry if you want it really authentic. Sherry is a good substitute but I feel like they were doing a disservice by not including the original ingredients. A 1/2 tsp of Chinese 5 spice and 1/4 tsp white pepper are also traditional ingredients that will amp up the flavour!)

OUTSTANDING!!! I have tried several beef and broccoli recipes I found online, and every last one of them was a disappointment. But this one….THIS is the one! Absolutely restaurant quality. I did sub sirloin for the round, because that’s what I had in the freezer. I also subbed Chinese cooking wine for the sherry. Other than that, I made the recipe as written. It’s going in my regular rotation! Note: one other thing I did that’s just a fun garnish: I actually grated the ginger and finely chopped the garlic. Toasted in oil and removed as directed, but set aside. Before serving, I added some pink salt and red pepper flakes to the toasted garlic/ginger, and sprinkled the mixture on top of my finished dish, along with some chopped green onion. It’s still delicious without the garnish, but that definitely put it over the top!

Just made it for the 2nd time. Chinese food is not my wife’s favorite and she loved it. I was actually surprised that I made this. I used low sodium soy sauce in the marinade (a lot of too salty comments) I used to work in a Chinese restaurant they always blanched the veggies so I blanched the broccoli for about 60 seconds but be careful putting wet broccoli in the hot oil. I used about a quarter cup of chicken broth (heat first in microwave) to loosen the sauce a little. I finished it with a dab of regular soy sauce pinch of salt and red pepper flakes. Oh almost forgot someone in the comments mentioned putting baking soda on the meat to tenderize it one of the best tips ever! I left it in the fridge for 2 days with the baking powder and than dabbed the meat with paper towels and then I cut the meat. So tender!

Lose the stereotypical Chinese music for the love of all things sacred!

Other than that, the dish was fine without having to discard the garlic and ginger. Chinese families like my hubby's would never discard garlic or ginger - they'd mince it or sliver it extremely thin to make it palatable to picky eaters.

I made 2 versions using real beef and Gardein Beefless Strips. I sliced a medium onion as well and used frozen broccoli that I cut fresh from the whole head and zip bagged in the freezer. So if you use frozen, sautee the broccoli before the onions.

I felt the sauce was too think, so I added a 1/4 cup of water towards the end, and added white pepper to taste for authenticity.

Best chicken and broccoli recipe around. Yes chicken. I have been making it with sliced or bite sized chunks of chicken thighs for years. The only changes I make is Increase soy sauce, garlic and ginger by 50%
Made as instructed but for subbing Miren for Sherry & increased sauce by 50%. My wife says we no longer need to go to the local Chinese restaurant & this must be added to the rotation. Outstanding.

This turned out great. I didn’t change anything except to add a handful of mushrooms that needed to be used up and that was a good addition! The only thing I would do differently next time is doubling the sauce, because I found that this amount of sauce didn’t really give the broccoli the tasty coating I was looking for.
I used the beef chucks rolls, frozen rolls that you would use for hot pot, I thawed them, put them in a bowl and cut with scissors into smaller pieces and it worked great!
It was great. I definitely would make it again. The only thing I change is I doubled up to sauce because I add mushrooms, water chestnut and onions in a 1 lb frozen bag of California blend vegetable.

I followed the recipe to the letter. It was bland. I double checked everything and all the ingredients were fresh. I intend to make more of the marinade to use with the leftovers. Hopefully I can prepare it in a way that will increase the flavors. Any suggestions are appreciated.

We loved this! Changes I made: added minced garlic and ginger in both the sauce and when stir frying broccoli. Added a sliced red pepper and 1/2 onion and mushrooms to broccoli. I think some red pepper flakes would also spice it nicely, and I will add a carrot next time
used Mirin instead of sherry and added more ginger when cooking the meet. also added yellow pepper on the last stage of cooking. was very yummy and will make again.
This turned out well. I am looking forward to making it again. Great Asian flavor.

This is my go-to recipe for broccoli beef. It is an easy to follow recipe. I replace the alcohol with apple juice and it works just fine. My family loves this dish and it really does taste as good as a restaurant!
Taste bland
I'd just have to cut back on the amount of oil. 4 or 5 tablespoons create a high calorie meal. But I love the flavors!
